pageCache.text:
Let your light shine
Welcome
We are delighted that you are visiting our website. We hope you find all of the information that you need but please feel free to give us a ring (01233 625531) if there is something else you want to know.
We are very proud of our school and enjoy showing people around, so if you are interested in joining our community, as a pupil, parent or member of staff, please contact us to arrange a tour.
Calendar
Our Church School
Ashford St Mary’s is a Church of England Primary School with it’s ethos and values underpinned by the teachings included in the Bible. In March 2017, pupils, parents, governors and staff voted on the Christian values that would guide everything that happens here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ashford St. Mary's Church of England Primary School - Google Classroom
pageCache.text:
Google Classroom
Google Classroom is an online learning platform developed by Google for educational institutions. The primary purpose of Google Classroom is to streamline the process of sharing files between teachers and students. Google Classroom is used from Year 1 to Year 6 in our school. Class teachers upload information and resources that can support your child's learning at home.
Accessing Google Classroom:
STEP 1: Get the APP or use a browser
You can access Google Classroom using mobile apps (Android & iOS), or via any web browser on a device or computer.
You are ready for STEP 2

Ashford St Mary’s Breakfast Club is available to all pupils from EYFS to Year 6. A healthy breakfast is provided and children are able to choose from a selection of cereals, fruit, toast, milk and fruit juice. There are also activities for the children to participate in.
The club costs £2.70 per day, per child and opens from 7:45am each morning. To allow time to eat breakfast children should arrive by 8am.

PE & Sports Premium Report
The PE and Sport Premium is a government funding initiative for primary schools in England designed to enhance the provision of PE and sports. This grant is aimed at helping schools improve the quality and range of PE and sports activities offered to pupils, encouraging healthy lifestyles and physical well-being.
Primary schools receive funding based on the number of pupils they have in year 1-6, with the expectation that it will be used to create sustainable improvements in PE. Schools are encouraged to spend the money on training staff, providing new equipment, increasing the participation of children in sports, or developing after-school sports programs. The Department for Education suggests that this funding is used to achieve long-term sustainable enhancement of PE and sport.
